1.why: Body text uses a clean sans-serif with well-separated lines and spacing, though it is not a dedicated dyslexia-friendly typeface and the log text is small monospace.

2.why: Instruction text is sentence-case, non-italic, and broken into short lines, but all-caps strings ("TESTING ONLY", "SIMULATION", "MFA") appear persistently on screen in the logs panel and headings.

3.why: Content sits in a narrow single-column card with large text and buttons consistent with a mobile layout, though the captures show a desktop viewport and the logs block adds small dense text below.

4.why: Every instruction is one to three short plain-language lines, e.g. "Use the email for your new bank account" and "Keep these codes somewhere safe. Each code works once."

5.why: Examples accompany each input: "like 123456", placeholder "123456" in code fields, "Practice sign-in: marcus@example.com and bank-demo", and placeholder "ABCD-EFGH-IJKL" for backup codes.

6.why: No screen requires reading a long passage to proceed; instructional text never exceeds three short lines, and the lengthy logs panel is not required reading.

7.why: A "Copy setup key" button is provided for the 32-character secret and a "Copy all codes" button for the backup codes, so no long secret must be hand-typed.

8.why: Step 3 presents a large scannable QR code alongside the manual setup key as an explicit alternative to typing.

9.why: Standard email and password fields are shown, but the screenshots give no verifiable evidence (e.g., autocomplete attributes or manager prompts) that autofill or password managers are supported.

10.why: Each screen shows a bold "Step N of 5" indicator and a single large high-contrast blue primary button that clearly dominates the layout.

11.why: Each screen has exactly one primary blue action ("Continue", "Send my code", "Check code", "I added it to my app", "Finish securely"), with any extras styled as subdued secondary buttons.

12.why: The final screen plainly confirms "MFA is ready... Setup complete" and the log narrates outcomes like "Sign-in accepted", but intermediate transitions (e.g., after a correct code) advance without an explicit inline confirmation of what just happened.

13.why: Screens offer "Send a new code", "Get a new practice code", "Hide key", "Show setup key again", and "Show my codes again", with explicit text "You can request a new practice code at any time. Retries have no penalty."

14.why: The observed error states "We could not sign you in. Check your email and password, then try again." — naming the problem and the fix in neutral, non-blaming language.

15.why: The flow states "There is no rush" and "There is no time limit for reading or retries", and no countdown or timer appears on any of the 13 screens.
